title: Principal-ideal Elkik approximation along a smooth open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $t\in A$ with $(A,tA)$ a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $B$ be a finitely presented commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $C=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}A/t^mA$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an open subscheme such that $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose an $A$-algebra map $u:B\to C$ induces a morphism whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}C\setminus V(tC)$ has image in $W$. Then for every integer $m\geq1$ there is an $A$-algebra map $v:B\to A$ such that $q_mv=\pi_mu$, where $q_m:A\to A/t^mA$ and $\pi_m:C\to A/t^mA$ are the quotient and coordinate projection. The parameter $t$ may be a zero-divisor or nilpotent.

source.place: Elkik, Solutions d’équations à coefficients dans un anneau hensélien (1973), II, Lemma 4, printed pp.564–566. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag is claimed for this result.

proof.text: First $t\in\operatorname{Jac}(A)$. Otherwise some maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ misses $t$; the finite $A$-algebra $A/\mathfrak m$ then has quotient by $t$ equal to the zero ring, whose idempotent has the two distinct lifts $0,1$, contradicting henselian uniqueness. Thus $A\to C$ is faithfully flat, hence injective, and $A\cap t^qC=t^qA$ for every $q\geq1$. The projection $C\to A/t^qA$ is surjective with kernel $t^qC$. If $t$ is nilpotent the inverse system stabilizes at $A$; then $C=A$ and $v=u$. We may henceforth assume $t$ not nilpotent.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 05CK (universally injective faithfully flat maps), and completion modulo powers; nilpotent case from the inverse-limit definition

proof.text: Let $T=\{x\in A:t^e x=0\text{ for some }e\geq0\}$. This is an ideal, hence has finitely many generators; taking a common bound for their annihilating exponents gives $t^eT=0$. Artin–Rees for $T\subseteq A$, $I=tA$, gives $T\cap t^qA\subseteq t^{q-k}T$ for $q\geq k$. Put $K=k+e$, so $T\cap t^qA=0$ whenever $q\geq K$. This bound, rather than cancellation of $t$, will remove the remaining relations.

source.place: Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees, applied to the finite module A and its torsion ideal

proof.text: Apply the conormal-chart lemma to $B,W$ to obtain $B\xrightarrow{i}D\xrightarrow{r}B$ and $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_N]\twoheadrightarrow D$ with kernel $J$. Extend the formal section by $u_D=u\circ r$ and write $a_k=u_D(p(x_k))\in C$. Since $ri=1$, its image on $D(t)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C$ lies in $W_D$. Approximating $u_D$ on $D$ and restricting along $i$ will therefore approximate the original $u$.

Choose an ideal $H\subseteq P$ whose image in $D$ cuts out the complement of $W_D$. Since the punctured section lies in $W_D$, every prime of $C$ containing all $g(a)$, $g\in H$, contains $t$. The radical characterization gives $t^\alpha=\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(a)$ for finitely many $g_j\in H$ and $\lambda_j\in C$, with $\alpha\geq0$. Lift each $\lambda_j$ modulo $t^{\alpha+1}C$ to $\mu_j\in A$ and set $h=\sum_j\mu_jg_j\in H$. Then $h(a)=t^\alpha(1+tz)$ for some $z\in C$. The element $1+tz$ is a unit: its inverse is the compatible sequence of finite geometric sums in $A/t^qA$. Thus $D_D(p(h))\subseteq W_D$ and the punctured formal section lies in $D_D(p(h))$.

Apply the chart lemma to $h$, obtaining $s,f_1,\ldots,f_c$. Write $\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_l$ for its maximal minors. Since the punctured section lies in $D_D(p(s))$, radical containment yields $t^d=\lambda s(a)$ in $C$ for some $d\geq0$. Since the minors generate the unit ideal after inverting $p(s)$, evaluating in $C[1/t]$ shows $(\Delta_
u(a))C[1/t]=C[1/t]$. Equivalently $V((\Delta_
u(a)))\subseteq V(t)$, so for some $g\geq0$ there are $\eta_
u\in C$ with $t^g=\sum_
u\eta_

u(a)$. Fix these finite certificates before choosing any approximation precision.

Choose $L$ with $L>2g$ and $R=L-g>\max(d,K,m)$. Use the completion projections to choose $a^0\in A^N$ congruent to $a$ modulo $t^LC$ and coefficients $\eta^0_
u\in A$ congruent to $\eta_
u$ modulo $t^LC$. Polynomial evaluation preserves congruence, so $f_j(a^0)\in t^LC\cap A=t^LA$ and $t^g-\sum_
u\eta^0_
u\Delta_
u(a^0)\in t^LC\cap A=t^LA$. Write the latter difference $t^Lz_0$. Then $t^g(1-t^{L-g}z_0)=\sum_
u\eta^0_
u\Delta_
u(a^0)$. Since $t\in\operatorname{Jac}(A)$, the parenthesized factor is a unit. Therefore $t^gA\subseteq\Delta(a^0)$.

The correction lemma applies over the original henselian pair $(A,tA)$ with $n=L$ and $h=g$: all $c$ equations have residual error in $t^LA$, their maximal minors contain $t^gA$, and $L>2g$. It gives $b\in A^N$ with $f_j(b)=0$ and $b-a^0\in(t^{L-g}A)^N$. Thus $b\equiv a\pmod {t^RC}$. No assertion that $A$ is complete, excellent or a G-ring has been used.

Lift $\lambda$ modulo $t^RC$ to $\lambda_0\in A$. The certificate $t^d=\lambda s(a)$ and $b\equiv a\pmod {t^RC}$ give $t^d-\lambda_0s(b)\in t^RC\cap A=t^RA$. Writing this as $t^Rz_1$ gives $t^d(1-t^{R-d}z_1)=\lambda_0s(b)$. Since $R>d$ the factor is a unit of $A$, and hence $t^d\in s(b)A$. Now $sJ\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ implies $s(b)F(b)=0$ and thus $t^dF(b)=0$ for every $F\in J$. Also $F(a)=0$ and polynomial congruence give $F(b)\in t^RC\cap A=t^RA$. Consequently $F(b)\in T\cap t^RA=0$, because $R\geq K$. Evaluation at $b$ therefore factors through $D$. Restrict this homomorphism along $i:B\to D$ to obtain $v:B\to A$. Since $R\geq m$, reducing evaluations modulo $t^m$ yields $q_mv=\pi_mu$, as required.
